dct_description_sm:
This dataset is a hydrological and geochemical monitoring dataset collected in the summers of 2017 (from May 25 to July 30, 48 days) and 2018 (from May 29 to August 17, 67 days) at the outlet of a gully system on Bylot Island, Nunavut (Canada). It includes measurements of stream discharge, precipitation, thaw depth, water chemistry, isotopes, and sediment concentrations.
It combines environmental variables (climate, hydrology, geomorphology) with biogeochemical parameters (nutrients, ions, isotopes, organic matter) to capture the dynamics of Arctic watershed processes.
dct_title_s: Thermal erosion and permafrost collapse boost carbon and solute exports, via surface runoff, Bylot Island, Canadian Arctic Archipelago
